result.title: GEPA optimization dashboard + agent chat replacement

facts.text: The old RLM agent (AxJSRuntime, SFL reply template, full-transcript memory search) is removed from server/src/routes/agent.ts.
The new chat agent answers session questions using typed tools that query SQLite directly: searchSessions, getSession (turn-range window), listInsights, getAnalytics.
searchSessions returns ranked snippets with session IDs, never full transcripts.
Codebase-graph tools are available to the agent only when the codebase-tools toggle is on; when off, they are absent from the agent's function list.
Chat replies are free-form markdown with citations that link to the cited sessions.
Conversations persist in SQLite; reloading the page restores the conversation.
A chat side panel can be opened on every dashboard page, and a full-width /chat page shows the same conversations.

The side panel sends the current page context (page type plus IDs such as sessionId, runId, versionId) with each message, and the agent can answer 'this session' / 'this run' without the user typing IDs.
Each page type shows context-specific suggested prompts in the side panel.
The agent has no tool that writes labels, promotes versions, or starts runs; draft outputs appear with a UI button the user must click to save.
Optimization tools (listRuns, getRun, getRoundDiff, compareVersions, getLabel) are added to the agent when their server routes exist.
Every CLI runner accepts a configured model: claude --model, codex -m, agy --model, vibe via VIBE_ACTIVE_MODEL, opencode -m provider/model.
The codex runner no longer hardcodes gpt-5.5.
A new OpenCode runner runs `opencode run -m <provider/model> --format json` and its output passes through the existing response parser.
Runners that support a reasoning-effort setting accept an optional variant.
A student identity is the triple runner + model + variant, and each analysis records the identity that produced it.
Each analysis row records the prompt_version_id that produced it (null = built-in prompt).
At analysis time, the pipeline uses the active prompt version for (target, current student identity); if none exists it uses the built-in prompt, never a version tuned for another identity.
Settings lets the user choose runner, model, and variant; model lists are filled from `agy models` / `opencode models` where available and free text otherwise.
A target registry defines session-analysis as the only enabled target; adding prompt-quality requires only a registry entry, no engine code changes.
A schema migration to v17 adds label storage; existing databases migrate without data loss.
A label stores: outcome, friction categories, pattern categories, key points, forbidden claims, optional note, split, and timestamps.
The labeling page shows the current production analysis for a session; keeping an item adds it as a key point, rejecting it as wrong adds it as a forbidden claim.
The user can type additional key points that the analysis missed.
Outcome, friction categories, and pattern categories are chosen from the canonical category lists.
Each labeled session is assigned train, validation, or test (60/20/20, seeded, stratified by project) at label time, and the assignment never changes.
A suggested labeling queue ranks unlabeled sessions for coverage across project, session-length bucket, and source tool.
After at least one completed run, the queue also ranks sessions where candidates disagreed most or test-gate scores were lowest.
SessionDetail has a 'Label this session' action that opens the labeling page for that session.
Sessions without an analysis can be pre-analyzed in bulk through the batch API (Mistral or OpenRouter) when the provider supports it.
Embeddings are used only for labeling aids (duplicate key-point detection, item-to-key-point suggestions), never for scoring.
View 7 (label progress) shows label counts per split, per project, and per length bucket against coverage targets.
GEPA evaluates candidates through the real session-analysis pipeline: same message formatter, response parser, and normalizers as production.
Only free-text guidance is optimizable; the JSON schema, canonical category lists, and output format are never exposed as GEPA components.
Scoring objectives are outcome, friction_f1, pattern_f1, keypoint_recall, faithfulness, and schema_valid; an unparseable output scores 0 on all objectives.
keypoint_recall and faithfulness come from a typed AxGen judge on the fixed judge model; judge results are cached by output hash.
The judge's rationales are passed to GEPA as feedbackFn text.
The regex heuristic metrics are removed from scoring.
One weights config drives both GEPA's paretoScalarize and version selection, so the saved version is the one selected.
The optimized result is applied with applyOptimization(result.optimizedProgram); the saved version equals the best candidate, not the last evaluated.
Validation examples are always the held-out validation split; the train set is never reused as validation.
Starting a run creates an optimization_runs row; the server runs one job at a time in-process; the user can cancel a running job.
Each round writes an optimization_rounds row with candidate component text, parent candidate, per-objective scores, judge rationales, and token cost.
A run stops cleanly when it reaches maxMetricCalls or its token/USD cap and keeps its best-so-far candidate.
The run form shows a pre-run estimate of calls, tokens, cost, and duration before starting.
The student is always the production student identity and cannot be changed per run; the teacher is selectable per run; the judge is fixed config.
Versions scored by different judge models show a warning when compared.
Transient API errors retry per call; a single rate-limit error does not restart the whole run.
Evaluation goes through one gepaAdapter with three modes: sync API, batch API, and CLI runner.
The run form has an 'overnight' toggle that batches GEPA loop evaluations; it is enabled only for provider:mistral or provider:openrouter students.
CLI-runner students always run synchronously, and the run form shows estimated duration and a quota warning.
The test gate scores the candidate and the currently active prompt (or built-in) on the test split, using the batch API when available.
Promote is disabled when the candidate's weighted test score does not beat the baseline, unless the user confirms an override.
Promoting sets the active version for (target, student identity); promoting a previous version is the rollback.
'Adopt for this model' runs only the test gate for an existing version on a new student identity and allows promotion without a GEPA run.
Existing analyses are not re-run on promotion; re-analysis is a separate optional action that uses the batch API when available.
The existing ~/.code-insights/optimization JSON manifest is imported into prompt_versions once, then no longer read.
`code-insights optimize` uses the same engine and tables, so CLI-started runs appear in the dashboard.
flow.ts, metric.ts, the unused template builders, and scripts/debug-optimization.mjs are deleted.
View 1 (run monitor) shows per-objective and weighted score lines by round, accepted/rejected candidates, cumulative tokens/cost, and a Cancel button, updating while the run is live.
View 4 (promotion gate) shows baseline vs candidate per objective, a per-test-session delta table, and side-by-side analysis outputs for any test session.
View 2 (prompt evolution) shows the candidate lineage tree; selecting a candidate shows a word-level diff against its parent plus the reflection and judge rationales behind it.
View 6 (judge audit) samples judge covered/violated decisions for the user to confirm or override and shows the judge-vs-human agreement rate.
View 3 (Pareto front) is a scatter plot with selectable objective axes; points are clickable and the selected version is highlighted.
View 5 (version history) shows each promoted version's test score over time and how friction/pattern category distributions in production analyses changed between prompt versions.
Each phase ships as its own PR to development in the order: agent, foundations, labeling, engine, insight views.
Server routes and DB functions for each phase have Vitest tests, and `pnpm run test` passes at the end of each phase.
The v17 migration and the manifest import are verified against a copy of the user's real database before merge.
